decisions.reason: Weekly reassessment. The 2026-10-30 docs now give a 90-day default expiry, reset only by upvote, with owner-configurable periods. The catalog says 28 days with use-based renewal. The fetched Memory pages state no release stage, so public preview is unconfirmed. Every gate stays unknown. Human dates are not renewed.

citations.quote: The expiry period starts when a memory is created and resets when Copilot upvotes it. Simply retrieving a memory does not reset this period. The default expiry period is 90 days.
On enterprise- and organization-managed plans, user-level preferences are off until an administrator enables them, after which you can opt out.
On Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans, user-level preferences are owned by the billing entity, which is the organization or enterprise that grants the user their license.
Organization and enterprise owners can export or delete user-level preferences for their members, either in bulk or per user.
Repository facts can be captured from pull requests that were closed without merging.
A memory disappearing from the list does not necessarily mean it has been deleted.
Disabling user-level preferences does not disable repository-level facts or delete stored memories.
The AI credits paid usage policy is enabled by default for Copilot Business, Copilot Enterprise, and Copilot access.

findings.reason: Docs say Memory is for all paid plans. The fetched Memory pages state no release stage, so the catalog's public-preview claim is unconfirmed. No tested client or pilot cohort evidence was fetched.
findings.next: Confirm the current stage from a primary source. Test a permitted and an ineligible pilot identity.

findings.reason: Docs say managed-plan user preferences stay off until an admin enables them, and repository access is controlled separately. No negative enforcement test was fetched.

findings.reason: Docs say billing entities own user preferences and repository facts need write access. Token and scope evidence, and out-of-scope denial, were not fetched.

findings.reason: Expiry is now documented as 90 days by default, reset only by upvote, and owner-configurable. This conflicts with the catalog's 28-day use-based wording. Facts can come from unmerged PRs. Residency evidence is missing.
findings.next: Reconcile the retention wording. Approve fact classes, test deletion, and review residency with synthetic data.

findings.reason: Docs say Copilot creates memories itself as a byproduct of work. Users cannot directly create or edit a memory. No review-before-use or prompt-injection evidence was fetched.
findings.next: Define a fact reviewer. Test an untrusted instruction that tries to store a harmful fact.

findings.reason: Docs say owners can export or delete user preferences. Memories carry citations. No sample trace, log retention, or incident reconstruction was fetched.
findings.next: Run a synthetic session. Reconstruct who created, used, and deleted a memory, and record gaps.
